replacements.claim: Because phi(0_R) = 0_S, the kernel is nonempty; together with closure under subtraction, this makes ker(phi) an additive subgroup of R. If r is in R and x is in ker(phi), then phi(rx) = phi(r)phi(x) = 0 and phi(xr) = phi(x)phi(r) = 0, so rx and xr are in ker(phi). Therefore ker(phi) is a two-sided ideal of R.
replacements.self_contained_claim: The kernel contains 0_R and is closed under subtraction, hence is an additive subgroup of R; moreover, for every r in R and x in ker(phi), phi(rx) = phi(r)phi(x) = 0 and phi(xr) = phi(x)phi(r) = 0, so rx,xr lie in ker(phi). Thus ker(phi) is a two-sided ideal of R.
